clue.text: They want fair play for sea freight terminals

definitions.meaning: people who play fairly and lose graciously

explanation.surface: A dockers' campaign for fair treatment at the cargo harbours.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair-minded players are called this, and the same letters split as harbours for merchandise.

clue.text: Something pointed in a joke that's wide open

indicators.note: in tells us the pointed thing sits inside the joke

parts.note: a pin is something with a sharp point

explanation.surface: A pointed joke that leaves things exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Yawning, gaping holes and mouths are opened wide.

clue.text: Having a row or swallowing a gin cocktail

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the combined letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Choosing between a quarrel and drinking a gin cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having a row' suggests quarrelling; it means rowing a boat. 'Swallowing' puts A GIN inside OR (OAGINR) and 'cocktail' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Propelling a boat with oars is rowing.

clue.text: Good men holding up English cathedral fashions

indicators.note: holding means the good men contain the cathedral
up in a down clue means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: Ely, the cathedral city in Cambridgeshire

explanation.surface: Saintly men supporting an English cathedral's fashions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holding up' splits in two: 'holding' is the container and 'up' reverses the cathedral city, since in a down clue it reads from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Fashions are modes or trends of dress.

clue.text: Twist the bad into an alternative setting

definitions.text: Twist the bad into an alternative setting

indicators.note: a setting holds a gem, so the alternative is put round the twisted word
to twist the word is to turn it round, so it is read backwards

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn wickedness into a different choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twist' reverses EVIL to LIVE, placed in OR. The whole clue also points at Dickens's hero, whose surname Twist completes the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dickens's orphan hero has the surname Twist, so this is the first name that goes with it.

clue.text: Public transport authority?

parts.note: not a transit body but the document that authorises a person to travel on a bus or train

explanation.surface: The body that runs buses and trains.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase reads as the body that runs buses; it is the slip that authorises a passenger to ride.
explanation.definitionFit: A travel pass is literally a permission, an authority, to use a bus or train.

clue.text: A structural expert from the Arctic

indicators.note: from means the expert is made out of these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A building specialist who comes from the polar north.
explanation.definitionFit: A designer of buildings is a professional in structures.

clue.text: They are mainly employed on tidying-up duties

definitions.text: They are mainly employed on tidying-up duties

parts.words: They are mainly employed on tidying-up duties
parts.note: 'mainly' means on the main, the sea: sailors who swab the decks

explanation.surface: Cleaning staff whose work is mostly housekeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mainly' looks like 'mostly'; it means on the main, the open sea, where these sailors scrub the ship's decks.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary seamen working on a ship's upper level do the swabbing and cleaning.

clue.text: A requisition kept by the police

definitions.meaning: the public peace that officers maintain, as in law and ___

explanation.surface: Police hang on to a request form.
explanation.definitionFit: A purchase request is this, and constables keep the peace, its other sense.

clue.text: Something said to impress a political splinter group?

definitions.meaning: a well-rehearsed turn performed to show off
read literally, a fragment of a political faction

explanation.surface: A breakaway faction's grandstanding speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsed showpiece at gatherings; read literally, a fragment broken off a political faction.

clue.text: Indian penitentiary filled with asphyxiating fumes?

definitions.meaning: a prison, a word brought into English from Hindi
making one gasp, so smoky and stifling

explanation.surface: A smoke-filled jail cell in India.
explanation.walkthrough: The jail sense is old British slang borrowed from Hindi, still heard in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglo-Indian slang for a lock-up, and also an adjective for air that makes you gasp.

clue.text: Old word made use of for the time being

definitions.text: Old word made use of for the time being

parts.words: Old word made use of for the time being
parts.note: describes an archaic term for the present occasion, also used of a word coined for one use only

explanation.surface: A dated expression revived temporarily.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic phrase 'for the ___' means for the present occasion, and a word coined for one occasion bears the same name.

clue.text: Improvised side that just scrapes along?

definitions.meaning: a team hastily assembled from whoever is available
a squad that barely gets by, scraping as with claws

explanation.surface: A makeshift team barely managing to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A hastily assembled squad is so called; read literally it is a group that just scrapes.

clue.text: He probably won't mind being laughed off the stage

definitions.text: He probably won't mind being laughed off the stage

parts.words: He probably won't mind being laughed off the stage
parts.note: laughter is what this performer wants, both on stage and off it

explanation.surface: A performer unbothered by being jeered from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'laughed off the stage' sounds like humiliation; for a stand-up, laughter on and off stage is success.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand-up entertainer welcomes laughter as the point of the act.

clue.text: The Scottish burgh in which Thomas Mann anguished

indicators.note: in which says the burgh lies inside the following words

explanation.surface: The Scottish town where the German novelist Thomas Mann suffered.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan's 'Maun' is a misread of Mann, the German novelist; the town spans 'mANN ANguished'. Annan is a town in Dumfriesshire, south-west Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Annan is a royal burgh in Dumfries and Galloway, south-west Scotland.

clue.text: Church tune designed to accommodate one

explanation.surface: A hymn written to make room for a single singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A seat built for a single person.

clue.text: I'm given a thumping and prevented from going astray!

explanation.surface: Someone complaining of a beating that stopped them wandering off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the pound for stray animals: impounded beasts cannot wander.
explanation.definitionFit: Stray animals are shut in a pen so they cannot wander off.

clue.text: Distinctive doctrines about different lines on weather-maps

indicators.note: about means the doctrines go round the other word

parts.note: isms are distinctive doctrines or ideologies

explanation.surface: Ideologies concerning the various lines drawn on forecasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Lines joining places of equal temperature on a meteorological chart.

clue.text: Feature of a seaside resort : that caters especially for machine operators

definitions.meaning: a seafront hall of games and slot machines

definitions.text: that caters especially for machine operators
definitions.meaning: players who feed and pull fruit machines

explanation.surface: A seaside attraction serving the people who work machines.
explanation.definitionFit: Seafront halls of gaming machines are a staple of British coastal towns, built for slot-machine players.

clue.text: Hardly the kind of rendezvous where old friends meet

definitions.text: Hardly the kind of rendezvous where old friends meet

parts.words: Hardly the kind of rendezvous where old friends meet
parts.note: a meeting place whose members are all young, so not for the elderly

explanation.surface: A venue unsuited to reunions of long-standing friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old friends' suggests long-standing friendship; here it means elderly people, who would not use a club for teenagers.
explanation.definitionFit: A club building for teenagers is no place for elderly people, the 'old' friends.

clue.text: Perks "for the lower-paid players?

definitions.meaning: film background actors, paid less than the stars

explanation.surface: Bonuses for the poorly paid actors.
explanation.definitionFit: Additional benefits on top of pay, and also film background actors.

clue.text: Sit up and beg for a paper handkerchief

indicators.note: up in a down clue reads the word from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to sue is to plead or beg, as in suing for peace

explanation.surface: A dog told to sit up and beg for a hanky.
explanation.definitionFit: A disposable soft paper hanky is called this.

clue.text: Omitting them leaves short months still warm

definitions.text: Omitting them leaves short months still warm

parts.words: Omitting them leaves short months still warm
parts.note: remove these letters from the last four months' names and the abbreviations Sept, Nov, Dec remain; also glowing remains of a fire

explanation.surface: Dropping something from the months still leaves them warm.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the shared ending out of September, November and December and the shortened forms SEPT, NOV, DEC remain. The answer is also what stays warm in a dying fire.
explanation.definitionFit: Glowing remains of a fire stay warm after the flames die.

clue.text: Entrance money?

parts.note: read as 'come in' turned round, money that arrives, as earnings

explanation.surface: An admission fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance money' looks like an admission charge; split the answer IN COME and it is money that comes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnings are money that comes in, so 'in come' describes the arrival.

clue.text: A meal service the abstainer takes comfort in

indicators.note: takes means the abstainer holds comfort inside

explanation.surface: A teetotaller finds solace in a set of crockery.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of cups, saucers and pot for serving tea.

clue.text: Address of a minister in a German service

indicators.note: in signals that the letters sit inside the words German service

explanation.surface: A German church service where a clergyman speaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Address' looks like a speech by a minister; it is his home address, the house of a Scottish Presbyterian minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The house provided for a Presbyterian minister is his residence.

clue.text: A symbol of power put at the end of a book

definitions.meaning: in maths, an exponent written above a number

definitions.text: put at the end of a book
definitions.meaning: the alphabetical list of topics at the back

explanation.surface: An emblem of authority placed at the end of a volume.
explanation.definitionFit: A mathematical exponent showing a power has this name, as does the alphabetical topic list at the back of a book.

clue.text: Thriving Shakespearian duke who did wonders with us

parts.note: Prospero, the magician Duke of Milan in The Tempest

explanation.surface: A successful Shakespeare character working his magic for us.
explanation.definitionFit: Flourishing and successful, doing well.

clue.text: Radiant smiles that can carry a lot of weight

definitions.text: that can carry a lot of weight
definitions.meaning: structural timbers or girders that bear loads

explanation.surface: Happy grins that count for a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad grins are so called, and so are load-bearing girders.

clue.text: Valuation as a group including élite Nazi troops

indicators.note: including means the group holds the troops inside it

parts.note: SS men, members of the Nazi Schutzstaffel

explanation.surface: Sizing up a unit that includes elite Nazi soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal or estimate of worth.
